definition: The same rule as bench/ground_truth.json: Y is a direct caller of X if running Y's own body can call X with no other repo-defined named function in between. Anonymous functions (callbacks, render props) belong to the named function or module that contains them, and are never a callee. Code that runs where a module is evaluated belongs to the module. Truth is what the program does at runtime, not what a static tool can see. Only repo-defined symbols count, tests included. A constructor call targets Class.constructor when the class has a constructor in source, else the class itself. Default parameter values are evaluated in the callee. An accessor pair shares one symbol, Class.name. Overrides are scored as bench/ground_truth.json scores S10 and K2: a call that reaches a subclass override at run time is a call of the override, whatever the receiver is (this in the base class, a parameter declared with the base class, an untyped value), so those callers are expected, not unresolved. The only callers taken out of expected are the three deferrals decided for v1 (an interface-typed receiver, a computed key or method name, a decorator) and the edges the tracer cannot see.
symbols: <path from the fixture root without extension, index collapsed to its directory>:<Outer.inner>. A module is its path alone. A const-bound arrow is named by its const. A test callback is <describe titles> > <it title>.

kinds.calls: from calls to: an ordinary call, `new`, a getter or setter access, or a callback passed by name to a library function (the library's own frames are not repo functions). A component React renders is NOT called by its parent.
kinds.renders: creator edge: the function whose body contains `<To/>` (or createElement) -> To. Children and render props are created where they are written, so the creator of a child passed through a wrapper is the caller of the wrapper.
kinds.renderer: renderer edge: the nearest enclosing project component in React's tree -> the component React invoked. A component passed as children is rendered by the wrapper that places it. A component React mounts at the root has no renderer in the repo and no edge.

unresolved: A query's `unresolved` maps callers that DO call the symbol at runtime (the trace sees them) but that ripple must not resolve from the source alone, to {why, site, reason}. They are checked against the trace and are not part of `expected`. why is one of: computed-key (TABLE[kind](x)), method-by-name (obj[name]()), interface-typed-receiver (a receiver declared with an interface), decorator (an @decorator line), decorator-wrapper (a wrapper a decorator installed calling the original through apply or call). site is file:line of the call, and its text must carry the marker of the why.
untraceable: A query's `untraceable` maps callers that belong in `expected` but that the tracer cannot observe, to {why, site, reason}. why is debug-flag: the call is guarded by a global flag the tests never set. The edge must NOT appear in any trace.
non_edges: Pairs that look like an edge and are not one. They must be absent from the trace, and ripple must not report them.
